record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: In the one-dimensional p-Laplacian boundary-value problem −(|u′|^{p−2}u′)′ = f(u) on (−1,1) with u(±1)=0, specialized to nonlinearities such as f(u)=λu^β−u^α with −1 < α < β < p−1 and in the parameter regime corresponding to condition (4.2), is there a unique critical exponent α* such that the problem has exactly one solution on one side of α* and exactly two solutions on the other side, as conjectured by the authors?

evidence.quote: It is reasonable to guess that there should be a unique α∗ such that there is only one solution on (−1, α∗] and two on (α∗, −1/p+1). We were unable to prove that this happens in general, but this is the case if the condition β = 1 + 2α is satisfied.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix p > 1 and consider the one-dimensional p-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
   -(|u'(x)|^{p-2} u'(x))' = f(u(x)),  x ∈ (-1, 1),    u(-1) = u(1) = 0,
with the nonlinearity
   f(u) = λ u^β - u^α,    u > 0,
where the exponents satisfy -1 < α < β < p - 1 and λ > 0 is a parameter chosen large enough that positive solutions exist (more precisely, in the parameter regime where the time-map associated with the ODE admits positive solutions and where, for fixed β, varying α through the interval (-1, -1/(p+1)) — sometimes written (-1, -1/p+1) — yields a transition in the number of positive solutions).

For fixed p, β, and λ in this regime, regard the number N(α) of positive classical solutions u ∈ C^1([-1,1]) of the above problem as a function of α ∈ (-1, -1/(p+1)).

Question: Does there exist a unique critical value α* ∈ (-1, -1/(p+1)) such that
   N(α) = 1   for every α ∈ (-1, α*],   and   N(α) = 2   for every α ∈ (α*, -1/(p+1))?

It is known that this is the case under the additional relation β = 1 + 2α. Prove or disprove the existence of such a unique threshold α* in general (within the stated parameter regime).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as an open conjecture; the authors note they could only prove it under the additional relation β = 1 + 2α. No web evidence was found indicating a general proof or disproof of the unique-threshold conjecture for the full parameter range.

status_evidence.title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption
status_evidence.snippet: It is reasonable to guess that there should be a unique α* such that there is only one solution on (−1, α*] and two on (α*, −1/p+1). We were unable to prove that this happens in general, but this is the case if the condition β = 1 + 2α is satisfied.
status_evidence.claim: The uniqueness of the multiplicity threshold α* is stated as a conjecture, proved only under the special relation β = 1 + 2α.
